reason: The cited evidence supports the general benefits of two-step heat treatments and sigma-phase precipitation hardening in Ti alloys and RHEAs, but it does not directly address the proposed Ti-Ni primary HEA composition (Ti30Ni30Al20V10Cr10) or confirm that the specific aging treatment will produce nanoscale, coherent precipitates with the claimed 20–30% strength and creep improvement at 800°C. The mechanism of creep resistance via precipitate pinning is plausible but not explicitly demonstrated in the cited passages.
premises: Two-step heat treatment (solution + aging) produces finer, more uniform precipitates than single-step in Ti alloys
Ni or Co addition to Al-Nb-Ti-V RHEA forms homogeneously distributed sigma precipitates upon heat treatment
Homogeneous sigma precipitates in RHEAs improve yield strength at elevated temperatures (up to 700–800°C)
Heat treatment at 1100°C for 1 h on Al-Nb-Ti-V-M alloys forms sigma particles that enhance yield strength
Nanoscale precipitates can pin dislocations and hinder grain boundary sliding, improving creep resistance
